summary: Jonathan Liew reports on England's Nations League win over the Netherlands at Wembley, sealed by Ella Toone's injury-time goal after England looked beaten after 35 minutes. The result keeps their Paris Olympic qualification hopes alive, though Liew notes long periods of poor play, defensive brittleness and a lack of cohesion and clarity. He argues the punishing post-pandemic tournament cycle has left the team frazzled, and they now travel to Glasgow for one last push.
one_line: Ella Toone's injury-time winner against the Netherlands keeps England's Olympic qualification hopes alive despite a largely poor, brittle performance at Wembley.
key_facts: Ella Toone scored an injury-time goal at Wembley, at 9.34pm, to earn England three points against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
The win kept England's Olympic dream of qualifying for Paris next summer alive.
The match looked lost after 35 minutes, with England having fallen behind to the Dutch.
Beth Mead replaced Chloe Kelly at half-time, and Georgia Stanway moved further forward and became a menace in the penalty area.
Toone and Alessia Russo came off the bench together, and Lauren James had a hand in all three England goals.
Lineth Beerensteyn scored twice for the Netherlands, goals of a kind England were not conceding four months earlier.
Jess Carter had a poor game and was replaced by Esme Morgan after half-time; Alex Greenwood over-committed for the first Dutch goal.
Mary Earps made a poor first-half error.
Liew identifies a lack of presence in both penalty areas, and problems with cohesion, energy and run timing, as the side's main flaws.
Sarina Wiegman talks often about defending against counterattacks, which Liew calls the key to England's whole enterprise.
England were still recovering from the trauma of Sydney, barely a month earlier, when they reassembled in the autumn.
England travel to Glasgow on Tuesday for one last push to qualify for the Olympics.
European Championship qualifiers follow in the spring.
